ADF test for retail sales with seasonality and trend break

dt <- read.csv("RetailSales.csv")
Retail_m <- ts(dt$Total, frequency=12, start=c(1982,4), end=c(2024,9))
logRetailSales <- window(log(aggregate(Retail_m, nfrequency=4)), 
                         start=c(2000,1), end=c(2018,4))
n <- length(logRetailSales)

  1. Simulating a time series under the unit root null and calculating the ADF test equation:

    library(urca)
# Set seed so the output is the same for each run
set.seed(42)

# Random drawing from ARIMA(0,1,0) model
Y <- arima.sim(n=n, model=list(order=c(0,1,0)))[-1]

# Compute ADF test with trend, print out equation
ADF <- ur.df(Y, type="trend", lags=0)
print(round(ADF@testreg$coefficients,4))
                Estimate Std. Error t value Pr(>|t|)
(Intercept)   0.4032     0.3308  1.2188   0.2269
z.lag.1      -0.0901     0.0492 -1.8313   0.0712
tt           -0.0060     0.0067 -0.9086   0.3666

    Replicating the ADF test equation using lm:

    # p: lag length in ADF test equation
p <- 1

# Observation indices for AR(p) model
t <- (p+1):n

# First difference and one lag of Y:
DY <- Y[t]-Y[t-1]
Y1 <- Y[t-1]

# ADF testing equation with linear trend
eq0 <- summary(lm(DY~Y1+t))
print(round(eq0$coefficients,4))
                Estimate Std. Error t value Pr(>|t|)
(Intercept)   0.4093     0.3368  1.2151   0.2283
Y1           -0.0901     0.0492 -1.8313   0.0712
t            -0.0060     0.0067 -0.9086   0.3666

    This implementation would be suitable for the purpose of calculating the ADF t statistic, noting that the t value matches for z.lag.1 and Y1 in the two pieces of output. You may notice the (Intercept) is slightly different – the reason is that the ur.df command uses \((t-1)\) for the linear trend instead of \(t\). To verify:

    # ADF testing equation with linear trend
eq1 <- summary(lm(DY~Y1+I(t-1)))
print(round(eq1$coefficients,4))
                Estimate Std. Error t value Pr(>|t|)
(Intercept)   0.4032     0.3308  1.2188   0.2269
Y1           -0.0901     0.0492 -1.8313   0.0712
I(t - 1)     -0.0060     0.0067 -0.9086   0.3666

    There is no clear reason to use \(t-1\) instead of \(t\) and it makes no difference to the unit root test, so we will follow the more usual convention of using \(t\).

  2. Simulation code:

    set.seed(42)
p <- 1
t <- (p+1):n
reps <- 10000
tADF <- matrix(nrow=reps, ncol=1)
for (r in 1:reps){
  Y <- arima.sim(n=n, model=list(order=c(0,1,0)))[-1]
  DY <- Y[t]-Y[t-1]
  Y1 <- Y[t-1]
  tADF[r] <- summary(lm(DY~Y1+t))$coefficients["Y1","t value"]
}

    1. Histogram:

      hist(tADF, breaks=30, freq=FALSE, xlim=c(-5,3))
x <- seq(from=-5, to=3, by=0.1)
lines(x, dnorm(x), col="red", lwd=2)

    2. Simulated critical values:

      SignificanceLevels <- c(0.01, 0.05, 0.1)
cv_sim <- quantile(tADF, probs=SignificanceLevels)
                1%     5%     10%
cv_sim -4.075 -3.458 -3.151

    3. Comparing with qunitroot:

      cv_trend <- qunitroot(p=SignificanceLevels, 
              N=n, trend="ct", statistic="t")
                  1%     5%     10%
cv_trend -4.083 -3.470 -3.162

      The simulated critical values provide a good approximation to those from the qunitroot command. The latter are themselves approximations, but from a very large and sophisticated simulation exercise. Increasing the number of replications in our simulations would be expected to improve the quality of the approximation for the critical values. Large numbers of replications are required to accurately simulate from the tail of the sampling distribution (1,5,10 percentiles) which is where the critical value are obtained.

  3. Simulation code:

    library(forecast)
p <- 1
t <- (p+1):n

# Setting up the X matrix of deterministic regressors
QD <- seasonaldummy(logRetailSales)
Time <- time(logRetailSales)
gfc <- 2008.5
Time_postgfc <- 1*(Time>gfc)*(Time-gfc)
X <- cbind(Time, Time_postgfc, QD)[t,]

reps <- 10000
tADF <- matrix(nrow=reps, ncol=1)
for (r in 1:reps){

  # Simulate under H0
  Y <- arima.sim(n=n, model=list(order=c(0,1,0)))[-1]

  # ADF test include X deterministics
  DY <- Y[t]-Y[t-1]
  Y1 <- Y[t-1]
  tADF[r] <- summary(lm(DY~Y1+X))$coefficients["Y1","t value"]

}

    1. Histogram

    2. Simulated critical values:

      SignificanceLevels <- c(0.01, 0.05, 0.1)
cv_sim <- quantile(tADF, probs=SignificanceLevels)
                1%     5%     10%
cv_sim -4.462 -3.860 -3.553

    3. Comparing these to those in question 2, it can be seen that including the trend break and quarterly dummies has shifted the sampling distribution and hence the critical values further to the right, i.e. in a more negative direction.

    1. The ADF test equation is \[ \Delta Y_t = \varphi Y_{t-1} + X_t'\beta + \sum_{j=1}^{p-1} \psi_j \Delta Y_{t-j} + U_t. \] Note that the lag length \(p=3\) implies that \(p-1=2\) lagged differences are included in the ADF equation. The ADF test statistic for log retail sales:

      p <- 3
t <- (p+1):n

X_ <- cbind(Time, Time_postgfc, QD)[t,]
DY <- logRetailSales[t]-logRetailSales[t-1]
Y1 <- logRetailSales[t-1]

# Setting up the two lagged differences of Y
DY1 <- logRetailSales[t-1]-logRetailSales[t-2]
DY2 <- logRetailSales[t-2]-logRetailSales[t-3]

ADF <- summary(lm(DY~Y1+X_+DY1+DY2))$coefficients
print(round(ADF,4))
                     Estimate Std. Error  t value Pr(>|t|)
(Intercept)    -27.6399     9.0084  -3.0682   0.0032
Y1              -0.2782     0.0814  -3.4188   0.0011
X_Time           0.0153     0.0049   3.1167   0.0027
X_Time_postgfc  -0.0056     0.0021  -2.6592   0.0099
X_QD.Q1         -0.2654     0.0144 -18.4255   0.0000
X_QD.Q2         -0.1620     0.0201  -8.0655   0.0000
X_QD.Q3         -0.0893     0.0191  -4.6759   0.0000
DY1              0.0017     0.1172   0.0144   0.9886
DY2              0.2171     0.1079   2.0121   0.0484
      tstat <- ADF["Y1","t value"]
      tstat -3.4188

    2. The 5% critical value from 3(b) is \(-3.860\). Since the test statistic \(t=-3.4187525\) is greater than this critical, we do not reject \(H_0\). i.e. we conclude the time series has a unit root.

    3. The p-value is calculated as follows.

      pval <- mean(tADF<tstat)
      pval 0.1323

      The p-value \(p=0.1323\) is not less than 0.05, so \(H_0\) : unit root is not rejected.
